hero.tagline: With the ease of a Markdown editor, the scaffolding of a classic writing studio, and an AI Agent for the whole book, it’s built to help you write your first bestseller.
star.thanks: Your download has started. If you like Drifting, star it on GitHub.
write.title: Writes like a Markdown editor
write.syntax: One quiet page and the keyboard. Type #, ## or ### to start an H1, H2 or H3; **bold**, *italic*, > and --- take shape as you type.
write.files: Every project is also a folder of Markdown files. Edit chapters and ideas in Obsidian or any text editor, and the changes merge back into Drifting.
write.transfer: Copy or save any document, or the whole book, as Markdown. Import .md, .txt and .docx.

studio.title: The scaffolding of a classic writing studio
studio.whole: Write chapter by chapter, or read and edit the whole book in one view.
studio.elements: Elements for characters, places, objects and lore. Patches record how an element changes, next to the passage that changes it.
studio.timeline: Storylines, a timeline in book order or narrative time, and a plot grid for each chapter.
studio.export: Export the book, or chosen chapters, as EPUB, PDF or Word.

agent.title: An AI Agent for the whole book
agent.providers: Bring your own key for DeepSeek, Anthropic or OpenAI, or sign in with a ChatGPT subscription (experimental). Writing never requires AI.
agent.edits: The Agent reads, searches and edits your project: prose, elements, relations, storylines, materials, TODOs. Its edits are marked in the text and can be undone from history.
agent.organize: When you come back after a break, it can file what you wrote into elements, patches and relations. It never edits prose on its own.
agent.mcp: Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity can connect to one project through MCP, read-only by default.

agent.prompt: The keeper says too much. Pare it down to one line, and leave Lin alone.
agent.answer: Done. The keeper’s line is down to one sentence and marked in the text. Lin’s parts are untouched.
data.title: Your data
data.offline: Everything is stored on your computer and works offline. No account needed.
data.export: Export every project as a Markdown ZIP, or back up the whole library as a restorable .drifting file.
data.deleted: Deleted projects stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days.
data.hosted: With an account you can sync between computers and share a chapter as a web page that readers can comment on. Synced projects are not end-to-end encrypted. See the privacy policy and terms.
faq.title: Questions
faq.compare.q: How is it different from Scrivener and Novelcrafter?
faq.compare.a: Drifting is a free, open-source app for Mac and Windows that works offline, with Scrivener-style chapters, outline, characters and research and an AI Agent that reads and edits the whole project. Scrivener is a long-standing desktop writing studio with no built-in AI; Novelcrafter is a web app for writing with AI, and needs a connection. Drifting keeps your manuscripts on your computer as a folder of Markdown files.
compare.agent: An Agent for the whole project, on your own key
compare.model: Your own key or a local model
faq.scrivener.q: Can I bring my Scrivener project?
faq.scrivener.a: Not directly: Drifting does not open .scriv projects. Compile the manuscript to Word (.docx) or plain text in Scrivener and import that; Drifting imports .md, .txt and .docx.
faq.offline.q: Does it work offline? Do I need an account?
faq.offline.a: It works offline, with no account. Everything is stored on your computer. Only the AI Agent goes online, to reach the model service you choose; an account is only for syncing between computers and sharing chapters.
faq.free.q: Is it free? Is it open source?
faq.free.a: Free to download. The source is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0-or-later, and you can build it yourself.
faq.ai.q: Do I have to use AI? Which models does it support?
faq.ai.a: Writing never requires AI. The Agent works with your own DeepSeek, Anthropic or OpenAI key, or a ChatGPT subscription (experimental). Local models are not supported yet.
faq.obsidian.q: Can I use it with Obsidian?
faq.obsidian.a: Yes. Every project is also a folder of Markdown files; chapters and ideas edited in Obsidian or any text editor merge back into Drifting. Export the book as EPUB, PDF or Word.
faq.backup.q: Could I lose my manuscript? How do I back it up?
faq.backup.a: Your manuscripts stay on your computer, with history snapshots, Recently Deleted for 30 days, and a backup of the whole library as a restorable .drifting file. Drifting is in early development: keep independent copies of manuscripts that matter.
faq.sync.a: Yes, with an account, which also lets you share a chapter as a web page readers can comment on. Synced projects are not end-to-end encrypted.
faq.system.a: macOS 13 or later on Apple Silicon, and Windows 10 or 11 on x64 or Arm (a preview for now). The interface is in English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, German, French and Brazilian Portuguese.
closing.title: For Mac and Windows
closing.notice: Early development. Drifting is used daily by its author and changes often. Keep independent copies of manuscripts that matter, and read the known issues.

closing.install: On a Mac, open the downloaded .dmg and drag Drifting to Applications (Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later). On Windows 10 or 11, run the downloaded installer: it needs no administrator rights, and a PC with an Arm processor uses the ARM64 installer. Choose your language on first launch.
